summary.one_liner: Open Interpreter is a Rust-based coding agent, forked from OpenAI's Codex, tuned to get strong results from low-cost models.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a terminal coding agent that is launched with `interpreter` or `i` after installation. The `/harness` command switches between emulated agent harnesses (native, claude-code, kimi-code, qwen-code, deepseek-tui, swe-agent, minimal, and others), and `/model` switches providers and models from the TUI. It runs as an Agent Client Protocol agent for ACP-compatible editors via `interpreter acp`, and it speaks the Codex exec protocol so the Codex SDK can use it as a drop-in binary override. It reuses shared AGENTS.md and .agents/skills directories, supports MCP, hooks, permissions and exec mode, and includes a built-in QA skill that drives web apps through agent-browser or native apps through trycua. Commands run inside native sandboxing on macOS, Linux and Windows.
use_cases: Run a terminal coding agent with low-cost LLM providers
Use an OpenAI-compatible model through Chat Completions
Plug a coding agent into an ACP-compatible editor
Swap Codex SDK backend for an alternative agent binary
Automate QA testing of web or native apps with an AI agent
Share AGENTS.md and agent skills across different coding agents
how_to_run: macOS and Linux: curl -fsSL <install script URL> | sh (URL is truncated in the README)
Windows: irm <install script URL> | iex (URL is truncated in the README)
Run `interpreter` or `i` in a terminal to start a session
Run `interpreter acp` to launch it as an ACP agent for editors
Run `interpreter --chat-completions` to use an OpenAI-compatible provider
notable: Harness emulation: `/harness` switches between agent harnesses modeled on Claude Code, Kimi Code, Qwen Code, DeepSeek TUI and others
Drop-in replacement for the Codex SDK via a one-line codexPathOverride
Portable design: uses AGENTS.md and .agents/skills rather than a proprietary format
Built-in QA skill for testing web apps in a browser and native apps
caveats: The README notes this is a new Rust version; the original Python project is now a community-maintained fork at endolith/open-interpreter
Live provider model lists require provider credentials documented in the provider docs
Install scripts are shown with truncated URLs in the README, so the exact install source is not confirmed here
